profile.summary: MIST (Metabolite Inference with Spectrum Transformers) is a neural network for untargeted metabolomics. It takes a tandem mass spectrum (MS/MS) of an unknown small molecule, labels each peak with a chemical formula, and predicts a molecular fingerprint. A second, contrastively trained model embeds spectra so that candidate structures from a reference list can be ranked for annotation.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: introduction; Nature Machine Intelligence abstract

summary_quotes.text: MIST models can be used to predict molecular fingerprints from tandem mass spectrometry data and, when trained in a contrastive learning framework, enable embedding and structure annotation by database lookup.
Rather than directly embed binned spectra, MIST applies a transformer architecture to directly encode and learn to represent collections of chemical formula.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each MS/MS peak is assigned a candidate chemical formula (subformula labelling), and a transformer encodes the set of formula-labelled peaks rather than a binned spectrum. The paper describes encoding peaks by their formula, implicitly featurising pairwise neutral losses, and training the network to also predict substructure fragments (the training command shows an auxiliary MAGMa loss). The fingerprint model predicts a 4096-bit Morgan fingerprint in the README example. A contrastive model is then trained on top of the fingerprint model with decoy molecules, so that spectra and candidate molecules can be compared by distance. Training also uses simulated spectra from a separate forward model (ICEBERG, from the ms-pred repository) as data augmentation.
sections.source_locator: README.md: introduction, Training models, Change log; article abstract

quotes.text: MIST incorporates domain insights into its architecture by encoding peaks with their chemical formula representations, implicitly featurizing pairwise neutral losses and training the network to additionally predict substructure fragments
After training fingerprint models, a single contrastive model can be trained on top of the MIST fingerprint model.
In the trained models and examples, external augmentation is conducted using the ICEBERG model (trained on same train/test splits).

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The default branch, main_v2, is an updated version of MIST, not the code of the published paper. Its change log lists model changes (internal subformula labelling, sinusoidal formula embeddings, a simplified architecture, Adam instead of RAdam, augmentation moved to the external ms-pred repository) and analysis changes (worst-case tie handling in retrieval, no ensembles). The quickstart downloads two pretrained checkpoints trained on the public canopus_train (NPLIB1) data: mist_fp_canopus_pretrain.ckpt and mist_contrastive_canopus_pretrain.ckpt, from Zenodo record 8316682. That record is titled v2.0.0, but its related identifier points to the v1.0.1 tag, and the record is not flagged as the last version; the sources do not explain this. A result should name the branch or commit, the checkpoint file, and the split file used.

sections.title: Use in benchmarks
sections.body: The MSAlign benchmark paper (an existing source on this record) ran MIST as a retrieval baseline and describes it as pretraining with fingerprint prediction, fine-tuning with contrastive learning, and augmenting data with a forward model.

quotes.text: MIST [26] is more complex model that pretrains with fingerprint prediction, finetunes with contrastive learning, and augments the data with a forward model for spectra simulation.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Supervised neural network that maps MS/MS spectra to molecular fingerprints, plus a contrastive model for spectrum embedding and candidate retrieval.

quotes.text: MIST models can be used to predict molecular fingerprints from tandem mass spectrometry data and, when trained in a contrastive learning framework, enable embedding and structure annotation by database lookup.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer over formula-labelled peaks. In the updated branch all inputs are concatenated once, passed through the transformer, pooled and run through an MLP.

quotes.text: MIST applies a transformer architecture to directly encode and learn to represent collections of chemical formula.
so that all inputs to the transformer are concatenated once, passed through the transformer, pooled, and run through an MLP.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: MS/MS spectra (an MGF file or .ms files) with a labels table that includes each spectrum's chemical formula; subformula assignments are computed from the spectra. Retrieval also needs a list of candidate SMILES.

quotes.text: we include an MGF file, `quickstart/quickstart.mgf` (a sample from the Mills et al. data), along with a set of sample smiles `quickstart/lookup_smiles.txt`.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Predicted fingerprints, dense spectrum embeddings, and ranked candidate molecules from a reference list.

quotes.text: 1. Predict fingerprints from spectra (`quickstart/model_predictions/fp_preds/`) 2. Annotate spectra by ranking candidates in a reference smiles list (`quickstart/model_predictions/retrieval/`) 3. Embed spectra into a dense continuous space

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not reported in the sources read. The README training example uses hidden size 256, 2 peak attention layers and 4 refine layers.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: The released checkpoints are trained on canopus_train (renamed NPLIB1), public GNPS data. The paper's main benchmarks used csi2022, which includes NIST spectra and cannot be redistributed. Training adds simulated spectra from a forward model run on unpaired molecule libraries.

quotes.text: **canopus\_train**: Public data extracted from GNPS and prepared by the 2021 CANOPUS methods paper. This has since been renamed "NPLIB1" in our subsequent papers.
We are not able to redistribute the CSI2022 dataset.
This dataset is used to complete most benchmarking done.
partially proprietary CSI2022 dataset that includes NIST

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: The published (paper) version and the updated main_v2 branch; Zenodo record 8316682 is titled v2.0.0. Two released checkpoints: mist_fp_canopus_pretrain.ckpt (fingerprint) and mist_contrastive_canopus_pretrain.ckpt (contrastive). The related MIST-CF predicts precursor formulae and is a separate repository.

quotes.text: This branch provides an updated version of the MIST method
MIST has also since been extended to predict precursor chemical formulae as [MIST-CF](https://github.com/samgoldman97/mist-cf).

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not stated. The Zenodo record with the checkpoints was published on 2023-09-07.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: Not stated as a model limit. The quickstart keeps up to 50 candidate formulae when it labels subformulae, which is a preprocessing setting.

facts.label: Weights licence
facts.value: other-open, as declared on the Zenodo record that holds the checkpoints; the exact terms are not given in the saved record.

facts.label: Access
facts.value: Code: https://github.com/samgoldman97/mist (default branch main_v2). Checkpoints: Zenodo record 8316682 (https://zenodo.org/records/8316682). Paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-023-00708-3.

strengths.text: Pretrained checkpoints and a quickstart that runs fingerprint prediction, embedding and retrieval on a bundled example are provided.

quotes.text: To showcase these capabilities, we include an MGF file

strengths.text: Code is MIT-licensed and the repository includes the configs and scripts used for the paper experiments.

quotes.text: **The config files specify the exact parameters used in experiments as reported in the paper.**

strengths.text: The authors report that MIST did better than standard neural architectures and a kernel method on fingerprint prediction for over 70% of metabolite standards (the authors' claim).

quotes.text: MIST performs favorably compared with both standard neural architectures and the state-of-the-art kernel method on the task of fingerprint prediction for over 70% of metabolite standards

limitations.text: The released code and checkpoints are an updated version that differs from the published paper, so paper figures may not match the release.

quotes.text: We detail changes since the published MIST manuscript.

run_guide.summary: Install the environment, download the two pretrained canopus_train checkpoints and run the bundled quickstart, which predicts fingerprints, embeds spectra and ranks candidate SMILES for the example MGF file.
prerequisites: The environment targets CUDA 11.1; the README says to comment that line out of environment.yml if no GPU will be used.
Tested by the authors on Ubuntu 20.04.1 with CUDA 11.4.
wget, used by the download script.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/samgoldman97/mist.git
cd mist
git checkout --detach 126649324655f00f8a8707f75a0c0492b11cbb4f
steps.explanation: Clone the repository and pin the reviewed commit. The checkout line is added by Rewire to pin the commit.

quotes.text: After git cloning the repository, the environment and package can be installed.

steps.title: Install
steps.shell:
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate ms-gen
pip install -r requirements.txt
python setup.py develop
steps.explanation: Create the ms-gen environment and install the package, as the README gives it.

quotes.text: conda env create -f environment.yml conda activate ms-gen pip install -r requirements.txt python setup.py develop

steps.title: Download checkpoints and run the quickstart
steps.explanation: The first script downloads mist_fp_canopus_pretrain.ckpt and mist_contrastive_canopus_pretrain.ckpt into pretrained_models/. The second labels subformulae, predicts fingerprints, embeds spectra, builds a small retrieval database and ranks candidates.

outputs: Predictions under quickstart/model_predictions: fingerprint predictions (fp_preds), contrastive embeddings (contrastive_embeds.p) and retrieval rankings (retrieval, with TSV output).
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The README notes that output predictions are included by default with the repository under quickstart/model_predictions.
The checkpoints are trained on canopus_train only, not the larger csi2022 data used for most paper benchmarks.

notes: The Nature Machine Intelligence paper is under exclusive licence and its full text was not read. The bioRxiv preprint (DOI 10.1101/2022.12.30.522318, from the saved Crossref search) would be at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.12.30.522318v1.full.pdf; the version suffix was not checked because bioRxiv was not contacted. The download script also lists Dropbox links for the same checkpoint names, overridden by the Zenodo links that follow. MIST is also used as the spectrum encoder inside DiffMS, FRIGID and MIST+MolForge records in this batch.
